$comment: The shrink-only STORY ratchet (#74), in the same shape as expected-parts.json.
scripts/run-axe-storybook.js refuses only a GLOBALLY empty story set. Nothing required any
particular story to exist, so a component shipping one `Default` story reported axe-zero
over one state and the gate could not tell that from full coverage. NFR-003 named that
defect in its own sentence — 'a component whose only story is its default state has had one
of its states tested' — and then supplied no mechanism that closed it.
This is the mechanism. Every story id listed here must exist in the built Storybook index;
a missing one fails the gate by name. Adding stories is free. REMOVING one requires editing
this file, which is the point: #74 deletes nothing, but it replaces eight hand-written
form-state HTML strings with element state, and the criterion that would have noticed their
loss was the one that could not.
Scoped to the ELEMENTS, not the whole catalogue. The thirteen packages/styles story files
predate this and pinning them here would be a ratchet nobody agreed to; #77-#79 migrate them
and can opt each in as it lands.

#78 opts sk-feature-card and sk-ribbon-card in. The a11y gate is what caught this batch's slotted-content contrast defect, and it is the ONLY gate that would catch a recurrence — so retiring these stories must not be silent. A lens noted four migrated elements were sitting outside this ratchet. These two are now in; sk-grid and sk-section-banner (#77's) are STILL OUTSIDE and are not covered by '#79 adds its own' — they need opting in by whoever touches them next.

#177 opts sk-card in, seventeen stories. It predated this ratchet, and the mission adds the stories the ratchet exists to protect — Greyscale and ForcedColors are the ONLY evidence that a status tone is not the sole carrier of meaning, and StatusCardComposition is the mission's proof that no sk-status-card element is needed. Retiring any of them must not be silent. Docs entries are excluded, matching every other element here.

#79 opts in its own three. The previous note said sk-grid and sk-section-banner were still outside and 'not covered by #79 adds its own' — two lenses observed #79 then added none either, so this per-component chore had been skipped by two batches running. FIVE element story files remain outside, not three: an earlier revision of this note said 'sk-card, sk-grid and sk-section-banner remain outside' and undercounted by two. The full list is sk-card, sk-grid, sk-section-banner, sk-nav-pill and sk-stub. sk-stub is the synthetic probe component and is arguably exempt, but nothing here said so, and a reader acting on the old count would have left two migrated elements silently unratcheted.

#219 opts in the FIRST styles-layer story: `components-card--statuses-greyscale`, one id, total 180 -> 181. The scope sentence four notes above — "scoped to the ELEMENTS, not the whole catalogue" because the packages/styles story files predate this and "#77-#79 migrate them and can opt each in as it lands" — has outlived its reason: those migrations landed and nothing was opted in. What replaces it is narrower than "everything" and stronger than "nothing": THE SCOPE IS THE ELEMENTS, PLUS ANY STORY A MISSION HAS NAMED AS ACCEPTANCE EVIDENCE. The principle, stated so the next mission does not re-derive it: a story cited as proof is ratcheted in the same commit that cites it. This id specifically, because #177's implementation-evidence.md names `Greyscale` AND `StatusesGreyscale` as its proof that a status tone is never the sole carrier of meaning. The element-layer half (elements-skcard--greyscale) was ratcheted by that mission; the STATIC half was not — and the static path is the no-JavaScript consumer ADR-10 section 3 exists to serve, so it is the half where a reader has no element to fall back on. The story your evidence names as proof was, for the static layer, the one that could be retired silently. NOT the whole packages/styles catalogue, deliberately: #219 raises that as an open question and it is a larger scope decision than a follow-up mission should take. The sweep that bounds this: kitty-specs holds exactly ONE implementation-evidence.md today (card-status-tone-axis-01M1VJNY), and it cites exactly one styles-layer story. When a second mission cites one, it adds it here, in its own commit.

#306 opts sk-progress into this ratchet for the first time. Five new indeterminate stories — Indeterminate, IndeterminateWithMeta, IndeterminateNarrow, IndeterminateLongLabel, IndeterminateForcedColors — are mandatory (#219's base rule: an element's own new stories). Four PRE-EXISTING ids join them because this mission's own acceptance-matrix.json names them as proof, not merely exercises them: Default and LightMode (FR-015 — acceptance-matrix.json's FR-015 evidence names both by name, as do spec.md FR-015 and NFR-002, plan.md and data-model.md (C-007 names LightMode alone, not the pair); the test that navigates to them, "LightMode resolves genuinely different computed track and label styling than Default", is PRE-EXISTING (#210, cited there against FR-011) and is not this mission's work — an earlier revision of this note wrongly called it new, and the diff offered in support of that claim (4422c83..7ae38fc over apps/storybook/src/tests/sk-progress.spec.ts) in fact shows no change to it — that diff was cited in the mission's report, not in this file, so do not look for it in this file's history. The citation rule turns on a mission NAMING a story as proof, not on the citing test being new, so the opt-in stands on the evidence field alone. Default is doubly justified: this mission's genuinely new absent-state regression test at sk-progress.spec.ts:390-418 navigates to it), and Complete and Zero (FR-008 — the new reduced-motion test at sk-progress.spec.ts:354-387 compares the frozen indeterminate frame's fill extent against both, per plan.md's own instruction to do so). The other five pre-existing ids — LargeTotal, LongLabel, Compact, Narrow, and the determinate ForcedColors — are deliberately NOT opted in: no spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md, or acceptance-matrix.json artifact in this mission names any of them as proof of anything, and #219 is explicit that the packages/styles catalogue is not swept in wholesale on that basis alone. Verified against the built Storybook index (primitives-skprogress-html--*) before committing, not guessed from export names; the autodocs --docs entry is excluded, as elsewhere. IndeterminateForcedColors and the reduced-motion baseline are the load-bearing pair beyond mere coverage: together they are the only evidence the indeterminate cue survives both forced-colors and prefers-reduced-motion, so retiring either silently removes that proof. total moves 496 -> 505.

#307 opts sk-action-row's static-path (`primitives-skactionrow-html--*`) stories into this ratchet for the first time, all TWENTY of them: Default, Collection, StaticTrigger, Route, Current, RouteCurrent, Flush, Card, WithoutMark, Sparse, SeveralControls, WithoutControls, RouteWithControls, LongContentNarrow, LongContentDesktop, RTL, Zoom200, ForcedColors, ReducedMotion, and LightMode. Each carries an FR annotation in this mission's spec/tests; apps/storybook/src/tests/elements-load.spec.ts:592 navigates to Current (`primitives-skactionrow-html--current`); and apps/storybook/src/tests/visual.spec.ts screenshots nine of them by name (Default, LightMode, Card, Flush, Route, Current, RouteCurrent, ForcedColors, LongContentNarrow — the mission's nine committed baseline PNGs). Verified against the built Storybook index (apps/storybook/storybook-static/index.json) before committing, not guessed from export names; the autodocs `--docs` entry is excluded, matching every other element here. #219's rule applies here exactly as it does to every prior opt-in this file records: a story a mission names as acceptance evidence is ratcheted in the same commit that cites it, and "styles-only, no sk-* element ships for it" (already established as NOT an exemption by #176's five styles-only primitives) does not except this set either — the static form IS the no-JavaScript consumer surface ADR-10 §3 exists to serve. The sharpest reason this particular set matters: `sk-action-row.markup.ts`'s own `PLACEHOLDER_CONTENT` comment records that an earlier revision of this exact default content used inert `sk-button--ghost` classes with no stylesheet loaded alongside, and axe caught a real WCAG AA colour-contrast failure against the dark surface on every generated exemplar and story that rendered it — fixed by the `color: inherit` rule the comment now documents. `scripts/run-axe-storybook.js` is the sole recurrence guard for that defect class; without these twenty ids declared here, any one of them — including the one that regressed — could be retired silently and the gate would never notice. ForcedColors and LongContentNarrow are load-bearing beyond mere coverage: ForcedColors is the only evidence the static form's forced-colors treatment survives at all, and LongContentNarrow is the only narrow-container-query reflow evidence; retiring either would remove real, not merely duplicate, proof. On the refreshed train after #306, total moves 505 -> 525.

The eleven remaining sk-boundary-page ids (FormCard through LightMode) are unchanged; none of the eight committed visual baselines ever opened `--default`, so removing it moves zero baselines. sk-boundary-page-responsive.spec.ts's theming test, the only other reference to the id, was repointed to `form-card` in the same commit.

#326 — 51 byElement keys was never 51 COVERED elements. sk-confirm-dialog, sk-grid, sk-nav-pill, sk-section-banner and sk-stub all ship real stories in the built index today and had no entry here at all, so their stories could be deleted silently -- exactly the loss this shrink-only ratchet exists to catch, for a set it had simply never been asked about. Four of the five are not a surprise: this file's own history above has said sk-grid, sk-section-banner and sk-nav-pill are 'still outside' across three separate revisions (#79, the #78 blog-card note, the #77 site-footer note) without ever opting them in, and called sk-stub 'arguably exempt' without recording that anywhere binding. sk-confirm-dialog never appears in this history at all. scripts/run-axe-storybook.js now derives the full ELEMENT set itself, from the built index's own 'Elements/*' story-group titles -- Storybook's category, not a second hand-maintained list -- and fails the gate for any such element that is neither a byElement key nor listed in unratchetedElements below, with a reason. Silence is no longer a state the gate accepts. The five below are recorded as unratcheted, not opted into byElement: none of them changes any rendered output, and inventing story-id lists for elements no mission has actually reviewed would be exactly the kind of ratchet-nobody-agreed-to the ORIGINAL scope note four notes above already warns against for the styles catalogue. byElement's 51 keys are unchanged by this entry; the total is 536 at this head, after #365(a) removed sk-boundary-page's Default decoy in the note directly above -- an earlier revision of this note said 537, which was true when it was written and stale by the time it landed.

#346 adds one to sk-progress's already-ratcheted set: primitives-skprogress-html--indeterminate-compact. FR-010 and data-model.md:57 declare `.sk-progress--indeterminate.sk-progress--compact` a supported combination, but no fixture, story, or assertion existed for it — the new IndeterminateCompact story is this mission's own acceptance evidence for that combination (#219's rule: a story cited as proof is ratcheted in the same commit that cites it), and the WP also carries a real layout assertion (row flex-direction, label/bar side-by-side), not merely a class-presence check. Verified against the built Storybook index (apps/storybook/storybook-static/index.json) before committing, not guessed from the export name; the autodocs `--docs` entry is excluded, as elsewhere. total moves 536 -> 537.

unratchetedElements.sk-confirm-dialog: Ships stories (elements-skconfirmdialog--*) but was never named in this file's own history -- not even as 'still outside'. No mission has reviewed it against this ratchet; #326 is the first time its absence was written down anywhere.
unratchetedElements.sk-grid: Outstanding since #79: this file's history calls it 'still outside' across three later revisions (#78, #77, #79 itself) and it was never opted in. #326 converts that recurring note into an explicit, gate-checked decision.
unratchetedElements.sk-nav-pill: Outstanding since #79, same history as sk-grid: repeatedly named 'still outside' and never opted in. #326 converts that recurring note into an explicit, gate-checked decision.
unratchetedElements.sk-section-banner: Outstanding since #79, same history as sk-grid: repeatedly named 'still outside' and never opted in. #326 converts that recurring note into an explicit, gate-checked decision.
unratchetedElements.sk-stub: The synthetic probe component used by check-elements-entries.mjs and the mutation harness, not a catalogue element a consumer picks. #79's note called it 'arguably exempt' but never recorded that exemption anywhere binding; #326 makes it explicit here instead.
